title: Why people starve
hookLine: people starve because rulers take too much (Tao Te Ching 75)

cards: A cheap T-shirt in a shopping cart. A delivery that shows up in an hour. A price that seems too good.
Behind each one is a person who carried part of the cost: the stitching, the late shift, the long drive. They don't appear on the receipt.
Chapter seventy-five of the Tao Te Ching reads that kind of receipt for a whole country. It looks at hungry people and answers a question that's easy to skip: who took the bread?

teach.b: The people are starving, the chapter says, because those above them eat up too much in taxes. No talk of bad luck or lazy farmers; it points straight up the ladder. Second, the unrest.
The people are hard to govern because those above are always doing things, always busy with their own plans. Trouble below is traced to busyness above.
Third, the recklessness. The people take death lightly because those above chase after life too greedily.
When the top grabs so hard at living, the bottom is left with so little that risking everything starts to look reasonable. Three problems, each traced to the same place.
Then a quieter closing line: one who doesn't make a busy project of living is wiser than one who prizes living too dearly. Fourth, the chain. No crown is needed for this.
Chains run through ordinary life too: a shopping cart, a payroll, a household, a group project. The chapter's habit is worth borrowing.
When something goes wrong lower down, before asking what's wrong with them, ask what's being taken from above, and who carries it.
And if life itself ever starts to feel that light to you, please reach out: in the US, call or text 988, or call local emergency help.

how: Readers of the Tao Te Ching often take chapter seventy-five as a sharp word to anyone in power: hunger, unrest and desperation below are traced to taking, meddling and grasping above.

games.q: you rule. your people are hungry and restless. where does chapter seventy-five tell you to look first?
o: at what those above are taking.
games.why: the chapter points straight up: the people starve because those above take too much, and are hard to govern because those above keep meddling.

practice: Bring to mind one ordinary thing from your day: a meal, a ride, something you bought, a task someone did for you.

Follow it back one step, to who made it, moved it or cleaned up after it, and let one face or one role come to mind, even someone you've never met. You don't need to fix anything; just let them be seen.
